---
title: Use the IOBRcausal Skill
---

The Skill lets an AI host turn your task into the package's public request.
Install it using the [installation guide](installation.qmd), then start a new
Codex or Claude Code session.

## Give the task and the files

In Codex, use `$iobrcausal`; in Claude Code, use `/iobrcausal`.
For example:

```text
$iobrcausal Inspect the expression matrix and clinical table in /path/to/project.
Check sample IDs and gene coverage, then plan a pathway-first Response analysis.
Use the baseline covariates in the supplied codebook.
```

For an already agreed execution task:

```text
$iobrcausal Run the agreed pathway-first analysis in /path/to/project.
Keep the approved endpoint, covariates, seed and testing family.
Deliver the complete endpoint tables, reading guide and figures.
```

For saved results:

```text
$iobrcausal Read /path/to/results and explain the requested feature's estimates.
Draw a forest plot from the saved numbers and include the source table.
```

Supply endpoint coding and units, sample IDs, matrix orientation and the actual
adjustment rationale. The host should inspect material gaps rather than infer
clinical definitions from column names.

## One execution entry

The Skill uses `iobrcausal(request = ..., inputs = ...)` with an explicit
complete-workflow request. Structured R requests do not need an LLM API.
Direct estimator chapters are advanced R instruction; they are separate ways
to ask a statistical question, not extra steps to run after a completed workflow.

The host integration uses the model access already supplied by that host.
Standalone natural-language calls from an independent R session need a configured
provider. Keep credentials outside scripts and reports.

## Optional package-managed integration

If the package CLI is available:

```bash
iobrcausal agent install
iobrcausal agent status
iobrcausal start
```

This is an alternative integration route with package-managed client assets.
Check actual host loading as well as installation status. The standard `npx`
command can install only the Skill documents before R is available.
Use [troubleshooting](reference/troubleshooting.qmd) if the launcher is not on PATH.
